source_text: Perfectus a Deo docetur de sollemnitatibus; inferior ab illuminatis. Duo modi doctrinae.
thought_title: Two modes of teaching about the festivals
orientation: Origen is introducing the section on the festal days, distinguishing two levels of instruction about the solemnities.
pass_a_gloss: Perfect [one] by God [is] taught about [the] solemnities; [the] inferior by [the] illuminated [ones]. Two modes of teaching.

choices.why: Keeps the masculine singular substantive force of the adjective, matching Origen's contrast between the mature and the less advanced.
Preserves the comparative adjective as a substantive, retaining the hierarchical contrast with 'perfectus'.
Renders the passive participle as a plural substantive, indicating those who have received illumination and can teach others.

choices.english: There are two modes of teaching
choices.why: Supplies the copula for natural English while keeping the terse summary force of the Latin nominal sentence.

pass_b_english: The perfect man is taught by God about the festal days; the inferior man is taught by the enlightened ones. There are two modes of teaching.
